The must-sees

10 places Wizzy will tap you for first, each with a story and something to look for.

  1. 01
    Building · 1836

    Arc de Triomphe

    Commissioned in 1806 after Austerlitz, it was finished in 1836. The Unknown Soldier was buried under the vault in 1921, and the flame has burned there since 1923.

    Look for

    On the side facing the Champs-Élysées, find François Rude’s relief of the volunteers of 1792, known as La Marseillaise.

  2. 02
    Building · 1889

    Eiffel Tower

    Gustave Eiffel’s company raised it in two years. Many artists called it a smokestack; it stayed, and it is still the tallest structure in the city center.

    Look for

    Below the first-floor balcony, the names of 72 French scientists and engineers are written in gold letters around all four sides.

  3. 03
    Museum

    Les Invalides

    Louis XIV founded it in 1670 as a home for old and wounded soldiers, and many of its buildings still serve veterans. Napoleon’s remains were brought back from Saint Helena in 1840 and lie beneath the dome.

    Look for

    Under the dome, Napoleon’s red stone sarcophagus sits in an open circular crypt, so everyone looks down on it from the balustrade.

  4. 04
    Museum · 1793

    Louvre

    The Louvre was a fortress, then the king’s residence, before the court moved to Versailles. The glass pyramid arrived in 1989 as the new front door.

    Look for

    Below ground, you can walk along the moat and stone foundations of the medieval fortress built by Philippe Auguste.

  5. 05
    Museum · 1986

    Musée d’Orsay

    The Gare d’Orsay opened for the 1900 exposition and closed as a station in 1939. It became a museum of art from 1848 to 1914.

    Look for

    On the upper floor, stand behind one of the great station clocks and look out through its glass face over the Seine to Montmartre.

  6. 06
    Church · 1345

    Notre-Dame

    Begun in 1163, Notre-Dame set the pattern for French Gothic. The 2019 fire destroyed the spire and roof; the rebuilt cathedral reopened in 2024.

    Look for

    On the square in front, find Point Zéro, a bronze star in the paving from which road distances across France are measured.

  7. 07
    Culture · 1875

    Opéra Garnier

    Opened in 1875, it was the social stage of the Third Republic as much as a theater. A lake under the building fed the Phantom legend.

    Look for

    High on the roof above the stage, a gilded Apollo holds his lyre up to the sky.

  8. 08
    Square · 1612

    Place des Vosges

    Henri IV laid it out in 1605 as the Place Royale. Victor Hugo lived at number 6; the arcades still make a complete circuit.

    Look for

    Find the two taller pavilions facing each other across the square: the King’s on the south side, the Queen’s on the north.

  9. 09
    Church · 1914

    Sacré-Cœur

    Built after the Franco-Prussian War as a national vow, it was finished in 1914. The terrace in front looks over the whole city.

    Look for

    Inside, look up at the apse mosaic of Christ with his arms spread wide, one of the largest mosaics in France.

  10. 10
    Church · 1248

    Sainte-Chapelle

    Louis IX raised it in the 1240s inside the royal palace. The upper chapel is almost entirely window, a lantern of biblical scenes.

    Look for

    The lower chapel, for palace staff, has a low vaulted ceiling painted blue and scattered with gold fleurs-de-lis.
